behavioral_laws.law: Part events announce index/kind, carry byte deltas only, then end once; accumulation is opt-in and invalid ordering is an error.
A turn ends with exactly one success outcome or terminal error and emits no event afterward.
Dropping chat/image/speech streams structurally aborts upstream work; dropping video attachment only detaches and cancellation is explicit.
Every dropped, emulated, or clamped requested feature produces one ordered unsupported record; fail-closed fallback rejects.
Context mutations require exact revision; truncate is explicit and never inferred from stale state.
Wire tool-call projection is turn-local, stable, collision-resolved, and reversible only for observed/emitted ids.
Namespaced properties use namespace/name keys and deterministic ordering; portable values preserve integer exactness through protobuf.
Multiple invocations may remain live by correlation id; inputs stream zero or more chunks and exactly one completion; cancel forbids later frames.
Successful output, usage, cost, unsupported records, revision, route identity, timing, diagnostics, and props form the authoritative atomic commit.
Image previews precede completion, speech chunks preserve playback order, transcription timings preserve request granularity, and video submit/poll/attach/cancel is durable job-shaped.
Protobuf is a process-boundary binding only; missing required fields, unspecified/unknown enums, invalid hashes/ids, non-finite numbers, and unsupported request forms fail conversion.
Absent optional controls preserve provider defaults; None and explicit empty extension/include bags remain distinguishable.

normalization: Rust type names are provenance labels only; behavior groups/laws are architecture-neutral.
